result:
Fixed `scenario.json` in place; the reader was right on the decoy failures, and partly right on the ambiguity.

What changed:
- Membership decoys 8105 and 8106 no longer sit outside all hubs (which made them fail c3 as well as c2). Both are now items of a new third hub, 8203 `Beacon Launch` (created by Priya Nair, last updated by Omar Haddad). Each now passes c1 (exact file name) and c3 (its own hub was last updated by Omar Haddad) and fails only c2 (it is not in the `Atlas Launch` hub). Their hooks are unchanged: 8105 still sits in the folder `Atlas Launch` (F2, `File.parent_id`), 8106 is still in Favorites (F2, `File.collections`). Query mechanics are unaffected — the `Beacon Launch` title keeps them out of the original query, and both mutations still select their witnesses.
- Explanations for 8105/8106 updated to state the `Beacon Launch` membership.
- Request reworded minimally: "...the Atlas Launch hub, which Omar Haddad last updated" (and c3 text to match). The non-restrictive `which` clause attaches to the immediately preceding noun `hub`.

What I kept and why: the updater condition still reads as a hub property rather than a file property. A file-side reading ("the file that Omar modified") is not one a careful colleague would take — the clause sits adjacent to `hub` — and, decisively, it matches no record at all (no file in the seed was modified by Omar), so no decoy meets the request under that reading either.
